newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. central and southern Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Monday were inactive, with no reported sales following last week's trade at $64.00 per cwt in that area, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids Monday were light at $63.00 and passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00, they said.

Fed cattle prices this week were seen underpinned by firm demand from packers working to maintain enough cattle inventories for the rest of the week and early into next week's holiday-shortened schedules, sources said.
Schedules next week were seen abbreviated by the U.S. Independence Day holiday on July 4.

Light support also was expected to be generated by showlists near steady with last week, with most feedlots current, cattle feeders said. Projections for firm cattle prices this week could be tempered by slower beef demand as retailers generally have finished stocking up for the holiday.

Beef prices were lower on Friday after surging higher the previous four days and weekly beef sales were lighter last week compared with the previous week, furthering ideas that retail beef demand was waning, sources said.
